Just now

--

AI coding is no longer a side experiment. It is becoming part of everyday developer work.
GitHub says Copilot Free expanded access to AI-powered workflows for millions of developers, and OpenAI’s Codex now works as a cloud-based software engineering agent that can handle tasks like writing features, fixing bugs, and proposing pull requests.
Press enter or click to view image in full size

Photo by Immo Wegmann on UnsplashThat is the real shift. AI is not just helping people write code faster. It is changing how code gets built.
Today, developers can use AI to draft functions, review changes, refactor messy files, and work across multiple tasks in parallel. OpenAI describes Codex as a command center for agentic coding, while Anthropic says agentic coding has taken off and that the share of GitHub projects with coding-agent activity has more than doubled since late 2025.
Press enter or click to view image in full size

Photo by Aerps.com on UnsplashBut this is not a “developers are dead” story. It is a “developers are moving up a level” story.
AI can speed up the boring parts. It can also help teams move faster. But architecture, product judgment, security, and debugging still need humans. Even Anthropic’s 2026 report says effective agentic coding still depends on supervision, validation, and human judgment.
The future of coding is not no-code.
It is AI-assisted code, built by humans who know how to direct it well. For more info — https://aimoneypro-jpat.arcada.app
